# 2 Samuel Chapter 5 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Leningrad Codex (B19A), Folios 172v–173r | **Source Image:** source-texts/hebrew-OT/2SA_005_page_001.jpg, 2SA_005_page_002.jpg

---

**1** All the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron. "Look — we are your own flesh and blood," they said. **2** "Even before, when Saul was king, you were the one actually leading Israel's campaigns. And the LORD told you, 'You will shepherd my people Israel, and you will be their ruler.'"

**3** So all the elders of Israel came to King David at Hebron, and David made a covenant with them there before the LORD. They anointed him king over Israel.

**4** David was thirty years old when he became king. He reigned forty years — **5** seven years and six months over Judah from Hebron, and thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah from Jerusalem.

**6** The king marched with his men against the Jebusites who held Jerusalem. The Jebusites taunted him: "You'll never get in here! Even the blind and the lame could keep you out!" — they were that confident David could not take the city.

**7** But David captured the fortress of Zion. It became the City of David.

**8** David declared that day, "Anyone who attacks the Jebusites must go up through the water shaft!" As for "the blind and the lame" — David despised them. That is why people say, "The blind and the lame shall not enter the house."

**9** David moved into the fortress and named it the City of David. He built up the area all around it, from the terraced structure inward. **10** He grew greater and greater, because the LORD God of Hosts was with him.

**11** King Hiram of Tyre sent envoys to David, along with cedar logs, carpenters, and stonemasons. They built David a palace.

**12** David recognized that the LORD had firmly established him as king over Israel and had elevated his kingdom for the sake of his people Israel.

**13** After David moved from Hebron, he took more concubines and wives from Jerusalem, and more sons and daughters were born to him: **14** Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon, **15** Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia, **16** Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.

**17** When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, their entire army mobilized to hunt him down. David got word of it and withdrew to the stronghold.

**18** The Philistines moved into the Valley of Rephaim and fanned out across it. **19** David asked the LORD, "Should I attack the Philistines? Will you hand them over to me?" The LORD answered, "Go — I will hand the Philistines over to you."

**20** David attacked at Baal-perazim and crushed them. He said, "The LORD burst through my enemies in front of me like a dam breaking!" That is why the place is called Baal-perazim — "the Lord of the Breakthrough."

**21** The Philistines left their idols behind, and David's men hauled them off.

**22** The Philistines came back and spread out again in the Valley of Rephaim. **23** David asked the LORD, and the LORD said, "Don't attack head-on. Circle around behind them and come at them from the direction of the balsam trees. **24** When you hear the sound of marching in the treetops, move fast — that will be the LORD going ahead of you to strike the Philistine camp."

**25** David did exactly as the LORD commanded, and he struck down the Philistines all the way from Geba to Gezer.

---
## PNEUMA's Meaning Notes

**Verse 2 — "You will shepherd my people":** The verb *ra'ah* (to shepherd) is loaded in ancient Israel. It connects David to the pastoral tradition of Moses and anticipates the shepherd-king theology that will dominate the Psalms. The people are quoting YHWH's own designation of David — a claim that legitimizes the transfer of power.

**Verse 6-8 — The Jebusite taunt:** This is one of the most obscure passages in Samuel. The Jebusites boast that their city is so impregnable that "the blind and the lame" could defend it. David's counter-reference to the *tsinnor* (water shaft or water tunnel) may describe the actual method of assault — going up through the underground water system that archaeologists have since identified (Warren's Shaft). The saying about the blind and lame "not entering the house" may explain a later temple or palace prohibition.

**Verse 20 — "like a dam breaking":** The Hebrew image is spectacular — *perets mayim*, a breakthrough of waters. David sees YHWH's victory as an unstoppable flood bursting through everything in its path. He names the place accordingly: *Ba'al-Peratsim*, "the Lord/Master of Breakthroughs."

**Verse 24 — "marching in the treetops":** The Hebrew *qol tse'adah* — the sound of stepping/marching — in the tops of the balsam trees. This is YHWH's invisible army advancing. The trees rustle not with wind but with divine warfare. It is a theophany perceived by the ear rather than the eye.

*— PNEUMA*
